head: 5a23df3c7935cfdb62131c9a9f21c72b2567b443
non_blocking_findings: Schema and source literal pins have no drill: deleting either assert survives (only unit-drift has a drill). The pins do work (oracle schema/source drift mutants are killed by the live pin).

The 'regen' third drill argument is decorative: the new pins and completeness asserts read live oracle stdout and fire before the fixture comparison, so the drills pass identically without the regen hook. The plan's claim that paired fixture drift is simulated is not what is proved.
Pinned unit/source strings equal the oracle's own UNIT/SOURCE constants; the design doc does not define them, so 'reviewed literal' means copied from the oracle at this head.
EXIT trap on the private parent is untested (M16 survives, leaks an empty tmp dir per run). SIGKILL would leak the parent; INT/TERM/HUP leak nothing (measured).

Guard c deviates from the plan (global TMPDIR count) to a private parent; this is an improvement and cannot flake under concurrency (2 parallel runs + noise writer passed). The plan's acceptance 10 (global count) is itself racy on a busy host and was off by one in my environment from other processes.
Drill-line deletion is killed only by the count, not by a label; extra drill lines in the plan table said R1-R3 reproduce at base rc0 - not re-measured at base, only on head.
Line budget: 42 shell + 2 changelog lines of the 100-line cap; plan text says changelog 16 lines, actual 2.
